classification.difficultyReason: Read each side by increasing stem values, derive its frequency pattern, and distinguish a high-value tail from two unequal peaks separated by a dip.

inlines.text: Describe the shape of each data set in the following back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot using the applicable terms: symmetric, positively skewed, negatively skewed or bimodal.

questionDiagrams.alt: Back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot of Mathematics test scores

spec.mathematics: All source leaves retained: blue counts3,5,3,2,2,1; red counts1,4,2,6,2,1.
spec.description: Native back-to-back stem-and-leaf plot with two continuous stem dividers and header rule.

answer.worked: For 9 Blue, the frequencies at stems $4$ to $9$ are $3,5,3,2,2,1$. The largest cluster is at the lower stems and the tail extends toward the higher stems, so the distribution is positively skewed.

For 9 Red, the frequencies at stems $4$ to $9$ are $1,4,2,6,2,1$. There are two peaks, at stems $5$ and $7$, separated by the lower frequency at stem $6$. The peaks need not have equal heights, so the distribution is bimodal.
